definition: Resentment is a lingering feeling of anger in response to an offense or wrongdoing. In this packet, it appears as an emotion that can be let go of through forgiveness.

provenance.scope: Source record D061347; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports the concept of forgiveness, defined as excusing or pardoning an offense or releasing anger or resentment, not a definition of resentment itself.
The claim that resentment is a lingering feeling of anger in response to an offense or wrongdoing is not supported by the supplied text.
The added statement that resentment can be let go of through forgiveness goes beyond the packet’s wording and is not presented as a supported definition of the term.

The packet text does not define “resentment” (it mentions “anger or resentment” as something that can be released via forgiveness, but provides no characterization such as “lingering” or “in response to an offense or wrongdoing”).

The definition’s claims about the source field (“cognition”) and the process (“can be let go of through forgiveness”) are not supported as a definition of resentment itself; the packet only supports that forgiveness may involve excusing/pardoning and release of anger or resentment, not the asserted nature of resentment.
